text: For every type E equipped with a normed additive commutative group structure, a real inner-product-space structure, finite dimensionality over ℝ, and a measurable-space structure whose measurable sets are the Borel sets, and for every function W : E → ℝ, assume that W is continuously Fréchet differentiable and that x ↦ exp(-W(x)) is integrable with respect to volume on E. Let μ be volume tilted by the potential -W, namely the measure obtained by normalizing the density exp(-W) relative to volume. For every partial ℝ-linear map D from L²(μ; ℝ) to L²(μ; E), assume that D is closable and that, for every u ∈ L²(μ; ℝ) and G ∈ L²(μ; E), (u,G) belongs to the graph of D if and only if there exists a smooth function f : E → ℝ having compact support such that a chosen measurable representative of u equals f μ-almost everywhere and a chosen measurable representative of G equals ∇f μ-almost everywhere. Then, for every u ∈ L²(μ; ℝ) and G ∈ L²(μ; E) whose pair belongs to the graph of the closure of D, their chosen measurable representatives, denoted ũ : E → ℝ and G̃ : E → E, are both locally integrable with respect to volume. Furthermore, for every continuously Fréchet differentiable function ψ : E → ℝ having compact support and every vector v ∈ E, both functions x ↦ ψ(x)⟨G̃(x),v⟩ℝ and x ↦ ũ(x)(dψ(x))[v] are integrable with respect to volume, and ∫_E ψ(x)⟨G̃(x),v⟩ℝ dvol(x) = -∫_E ũ(x)(dψ(x))[v] dvol(x). Here dψ(x) is the real Fréchet derivative of ψ at x. This conclusion is only a forward implication from membership in the closed graph to the stated local integrability and distributional-gradient identity; no converse characterization of that graph is asserted.
